dhp290:1: If by renouncing some trifling pleasure one can obtain pleasure abounding,
dhp290:3: A wise man should consider pleasure abounding and renounce the trifling pleasure.
dhp291:1: Whoever by causing suffering to others seeks to win happiness for himself,
dhp291:3: Becomes entangled in the bonds of hate; such a man is never freed from hatred.
dhp292:1: For that which should be done is left undone;
dhp292:2: And that is done which should be left undone;
dhp292:3: The Impurities of the arrogant and heedless ever increase.
dhp293:1: But they that ever devote themselves to Meditation on the Body,
dhp293:2: They follow not after that which should be left undone,
dhp293:4: But persevere in that which should be done;
dhp293:5: The Impurities of the thoughtful and intelligent come to an end.
dhp294:1: After killing a mother and a father, and two kings of the Warrior caste,
dhp294:3: After destroying a kingdom with its inhabitants, scatheless goes the Brahman.
dhp295:1: After killing a mother and a father, two Brahman kings,
dhp295:3: And an eminent man besides, scatheless goes the Brahman.
dhp296:1: Well awake and watchful ever are the disciples of Gotama,
dhp296:3: They that meditate constantly, both by day and by night, on the Buddha.
dhp297:1: Well awake and watchful ever are the disciples of Gotama,
dhp297:3: They that meditate constantly, both by day and by night, on the Law.
dhp298:1: Well awake and watchful ever are the disciples of Gotama,
dhp298:3: They that meditate constantly, both by day and by night, on the Order.
dhp299:1: Well awake and watchful ever are the disciples of Gotama,
dhp299:3: They that meditate constantly, both by day and by night, on the body.
dhp300:1: Well awake and watchful ever are the disciples of Gotama,
dhp300:3: They whose minds delight, both by day and by night, in non-injury.
dhp301:1: Well awake and watchful ever are the disciples of Gotama,
dhp301:3: They whose minds delight, both by day and by night, in meditation.
dhp302:1: Fraught with hardship is the life of a monk, and hard to enjoy.
dhp302:2: Fraught with hardship is life in the world. Houses are painful to live in.
dhp302:4: Painful is it to dwell together with unequals. Suffering follows wayfarers in the round of existences.
dhp302:5: Therefore one should not be such a wayfarer; one should not let suffering follow him.
dhp303:1: If a man be faithful, endued with virtue, possessed of fame and wealth,
dhp303:3: He may go to what place he will, and there, wherever it may be, he is honored.
dhp304:1: From afar are manifest the good, like the Himalaya mountains;
dhp304:3: They that lack goodness are not seen here, like arrows shot in darkness.
dhp305:1: He who sits alone, lodges alone, and walks alone, unwearied,
dhp305:3: He who, alone, subdues himself, such a man will delight in the outskirts of the forest.
